blocks.title: Complementary MOS (CMOS) Inverter
blocks.body: The standard building block of digital VLSI circuits, consisting of a pull-up PMOS network and a pull-down NMOS network with shared input gates and tied drain outputs. Exhibits negligible static power dissipation and rail-to-rail output swing.

Short-Circuit Power During Transitions
blocks.body: During switching, both NMOS and PMOS conduct simultaneously for a brief duration when $V_{th,n} < V_{in} < V_{DD} - |V_{th,p}|$, creating a direct current spike from $V_{DD}$ to ground.

points: Static power consumption is practically zero, dominated only by reverse leakage current.
Dynamic power dissipation scales quadratically with supply voltage $V_{DD}$.

questions: Why must PMOS width $W_p$ typically be 2 to 3 times larger than NMOS width $W_n$ for symmetric propagation delays?
How does reducing supply voltage $V_{DD}$ affect propagation delay versus energy efficiency?
